## Task input
# Task: Add a serial test mode — `./visual-relay test serial [Filter]`

The parallel suite's per-test timings are unusable for finding slow tests. Add
an opt-in serial mode that runs test collections one at a time so a timing run
produces trustworthy per-test numbers. Default behavior must not change.

### Evidence (2026-07-19 slow-test investigation)

- `tests/VisualRelay.Tests/xunit.runner.json` sets `parallelizeTestCollections:
  true`, `maxParallelThreads: "2.0x"`, `parallelAlgorithm: "aggressive"`. In a
  full-suite TRX the per-test durations sum to ~5,200s inside ~92s of wall
  clock (host run `test-logs/20260712T222826_Mac_17600.trx`: 3,174 tests, sum
  5,204s, wall 91s; VM run `20260718T124658_…_5259.trx`: 3,306 tests, sum
  5,194s, wall 92s). A test's reported duration is dominated by time queued
  between awaits, not work.
- Concrete: `RelayDriverVerifyFixTests.RunTaskAsync_VerifyGreen_…` reported
  29s in a full host run but measures 0.016s in a filtered class run;
  `ControlServerKestrelHandlerTests.UnknownRoute_Returns404_Json` swung 0.0s ↔
  20s between two full runs. See attached `investigation-baseline.md`.
- `tools/VisualRelay.Cli/TestRunner.cs:38-47` — a leading non-flag token
  becomes the `FullyQualifiedName~` filter; remaining args are forwarded to
  `dotnet test` verbatim.
- xunit accepts RunSettings overrides as inline `dotnet test` arguments after
  `--`, e.g. `dotnet test -- xUnit.ParallelizeTestCollections=false`
  (https://xunit.net/docs/runsettings; the repo uses xunit.v3 +
  xunit.runner.visualstudio 3.1.5, which honor the `xUnit.*` keys).
- `tools/VisualRelay.Cli/WatchdogTimeouts.cs:12-13` — the test watchdog
  defaults to 60s (`VISUAL_RELAY_TEST_TIMEOUT` overrides). A serial full suite
  will exceed 60s by construction (the parallel run already takes ~92s).

### What to build

Exactly this shape, in `tools/VisualRelay.Cli/TestRunner.cs`:

1. Extract the argument construction into a pure, testable
   `internal static` builder (e.g. `BuildTestArgs(...)`) that `RunAsync` calls.
   Keep behavior byte-identical for existing inputs.
2. Recognize the literal first token `serial` (ordinal comparison): consume
   it and set serial mode. After consuming it, the existing rule applies
   unchanged to the remaining tokens — a next non-flag token becomes the
   filter, the rest are forwarded. `./visual-relay test serial`,
   `./visual-relay test serial GitCommitter`, and `./visual-relay test
   GitCommitter` must all work.
3. In serial mode append the RunSettings tail as the final arguments:
   `--` then `xUnit.ParallelizeTestCollections=false`. Tests within a
   collection already run sequentially, so this one key yields a fully serial
   run. Do not modify `xunit.runner.json` (the default run keeps its
   parallelism).
4. In serial mode, when `VISUAL_RELAY_TEST_TIMEOUT` is unset, use a 1800s
   watchdog default instead of 60s (add a serial-aware resolver next to
   `WatchdogTimeouts.ForTest()`; the env var still wins when set).
5. Print one stderr line when serial mode is active, alongside the existing
   log-path lines, e.g. `serial mode: one collection at a time; per-test
   timings are trustworthy`.
6. Update the CLI usage/help text where `test` is documented (grep the CLI
   project for the existing `test` usage string) and add a short note to the
   test-runner section of `TROUBLESHOOTING.md` saying serial mode exists and
   what it is for.

Out of scope: combining `serial` with a caller-supplied `--` RunSettings tail;
if the forwarded args already contain `--`, fail with a clear error rather
than merging.

### Constraints

- Default (non-serial) invocations must produce byte-identical `dotnet test`
  arguments to today — prove it with the builder tests.
- No new dependencies; keep files under the 300-line guard.
- Coverage is non-negotiable: no test is deleted, skipped, or weakened.

### Tests (red first)

In a new `CliSerialTestModeTests` (pattern: `CliTestLogPathsTests`):

- `serial` leading token → args end with `--` followed by
  `xUnit.ParallelizeTestCollections=false`, and no
  `FullyQualifiedName~serial` filter is present.
- `serial GitCommitter` → both the RunSettings tail and
  `--filter FullyQualifiedName~GitCommitter` are present.
- `GitCommitter` alone → args identical to today's (no RunSettings tail).
- Serial + `VISUAL_RELAY_TEST_TIMEOUT` unset → 1800s; set to `90` → 90s
  (exercise the pure `Resolve`-style seam, not process-global env state).

### Verification

- `./visual-relay check` fully green.
- Manual: `./visual-relay test serial CliSerialTestModeTests` runs and the
  stderr note appears; `NO_BUILD=1 ./visual-relay test serial` completes a
  full serial suite without tripping the watchdog.

### Commit-message evidence

Measure before and after while implementing (a serial run's wall time vs the
parallel run's is the natural pair), then put one filled-in evidence bullet in
the commit message body, following the attached `commit-message-evidence.md`.
Never pre-fill that bullet — numbers are measured at implementation time and
go into the eventual commit message, nowhere else.

# Commit-message evidence for test-speed changes

Any commit that changes how long tests take must carry, in its commit-message
body, exactly one bullet of this shape, blanks filled with real measurements:

- test time dropped from <before> to <after>, saving <delta> (<scope>)

How to fill it in:

- `<before>` / `<after>`: numbers you measured yourself, on this machine, with
  the same command, once right before starting and once right after finishing.
  Never copy them from a task description, an estimate, or a prediction.
- `<delta>`: the difference between the two.
- `<scope>`: what the numbers cover: `full-suite wall time`, `single test`, or
  `<TestClass> file total`.
- A finished example:
  `- test time dropped from 80s to 60s, saving 20s (full-suite wall time)`

Rules:

- The filled-in bullet belongs in the commit message body, never in a task
  file. A task file states the requirement; only the commit records numbers.
- Exactly one evidence bullet per commit. The commit hook allows at most 3
  body bullets of at most 20 words each, all `- ` hyphen bullets, no em
  dashes; keep the evidence bullet well inside those limits.
- If you cannot measure a real improvement, say so in your run summary and do
  not invent numbers. A commit with no measured effect gets no evidence bullet.

Here is the diagnosis, grounded in the current code at HEAD (16f5bf0).

---

## Evidence

### 1. Argument construction is inlined — no extraction point exists

`TestRunner.RunAsync` (112 lines) builds the `dotnet test` argument list inline at lines 26–47. There is no separate builder method, so a serial-mode flag cannot be injected without touching the core construction logic. The block:

```
26: var testArgs = new List<string> { "test", paths.TestsProject, "-m:1", … };
35: if (NO_BUILD) testArgs.Add("--no-build");
38-47: // filter extraction + forwarded args
49: var timeout = WatchdogTimeouts.ForTest();
```

Every piece — base args, NO_BUILD, filter, forwarding — is hard-coded in `RunAsync`. To add serial mode, the arg construction must first be extracted into a pure method so the serial flag can be consumed and the `-- xUnit.ParallelizeTestCollections=false` tail can be appended without duplicating the existing logic.

### 2. No serial-detection token exists

The CLI accepts `./visual-relay test [args...]`. `TestCommand.RunAsync` (10 lines, thin delegate) forwards directly to `TestRunner.RunAsync`. There is no token recognition before the filter logic runs. The first non-flag token is always treated as a `FullyQualifiedName~` filter (line 41). Adding `serial` recognition requires an ordinal comparison check *before* the filter logic, consuming the token if matched.

### 3. Watchdog default is hard-coded to 60s with no serial awareness

`WatchdogTimeouts.ForTest()` at line 12–13:

```csharp
public static TimeSpan ForTest() =>
    Resolve(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("VISUAL_RELAY_TEST_TIMEOUT"), 60);
```

The default of 60s is correct for the parallel suite (~92s wall clock means no individual `dotnet test` process exceeds 60s), but a serial full suite will take much longer (the parallel run is already ~92s; serial will be many minutes). A 1800s default is needed, but only when serial mode is active. The env var must still win when set. The pure `Resolve(string?, int)` seam at line 22 is already testable — the serial variant needs only to supply a different default.

### 4. Usage text and docs are silent about serial mode

`CommandRouter.UsageLine` (line 21–23) lists `test` among commands with no hint of `serial`:

```
"usage: ./visual-relay [launch|build|test|format|screenshot|run-task|init|" +
"install-hooks|bump-version|check|inspect|guards|audit|gen-backend-config|provision-mxc]"
```

`TROUBLESHOOTING.md` (102 lines) has a "test run hangs" section (lines 5–22) that mentions `--blame-hang` and the timeout env var, but nothing about serial mode for trustworthy per-test timings.

### 5. `--` conflict: no detection exists

The current forwarding logic at line 47 (`testArgs.AddRange(forwarded)`) passes everything through to `dotnet test` verbatim. If a caller supplies `-- someRunSetting` alongside serial mode, the builder would append a second `-- xUnit.ParallelizeTestCollections=false`, producing two `--` separators. xUnit's argument parser would see only the first `--` and treat the second as a test filter, not a RunSettings key. The task requires a clear error rather than silent misbehavior.

### 6. No `InternalsVisibleTo` — all tested types are `public`

The CLI project (`VisualRelay.Cli.csproj`) has no `[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo]`. Every type tested from `VisualRelay.Tests` (`TestLogPaths`, `WatchdogTimeouts`, `TimeoutWatchdog`, `CommandRouter`) is declared `public`. The new `BuildTestArgs` must either be `public` or the project must add `InternalsVisibleTo("VisualRelay.Tests")`. The task says `internal static`; the project needs the attribute regardless.

### 7. Test file shape is clear from precedent

`CliTestLogPathsTests` (50 lines) and `CliWatchdogTests` (83 lines) establish the pattern: `public sealed class` in `namespace VisualRelay.Tests;`, `using VisualRelay.Cli;`, `[Fact]`/`[Theory]` attributes, no constructor, no `IClassFixture`. The new `CliSerialTestModeTests` follows the same shape.

### 8. Line-count guard is satisfied

| File | Current | After |
|---|---|---|
| `TestRunner.cs` | 112 | ~155 |
| `WatchdogTimeouts.cs` | 28 | ~35 |
| `CommandRouter.cs` | 24 | ~25 |
| `TROUBLESHOOTING.md` | 102 | ~107 |
| New `CliSerialTestModeTests.cs` | 0 | ~80 |

All well under 300.

---

## Excerpts

### TestRunner.cs:26-50 — the extraction target
```csharp
var testArgs = new List<string>
{
    "test", paths.TestsProject,
    "-m:1", "-p:UseSharedCompilation=false",
    "--logger", "console;verbosity=normal",
    "--logger", $"trx;LogFileName={log.Stem}.trx",
    "--results-directory", logDir,
};

if (string.Equals(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("NO_BUILD"), "1", StringComparison.Ordinal))
    testArgs.Add("--no-build");

var forwarded = new List<string>(args);
if (forwarded.Count > 0 && !forwarded[0].StartsWith('-'))
{
    testArgs.Add("--filter");
    testArgs.Add($"FullyQualifiedName~{forwarded[0]}");
    forwarded.RemoveAt(0);
}
testArgs.AddRange(forwarded);

var timeout = WatchdogTimeouts.ForTest();
```

### WatchdogTimeouts.cs:12-13 — the hard-coded 60s default
```csharp
public static TimeSpan ForTest() =>
    Resolve(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("VISUAL_RELAY_TEST_TIMEOUT"), 60);
```

### WatchdogTimeouts.cs:22-27 — the pure Resolve seam (already testable)
```csharp
public static TimeSpan Resolve(string? rawValue, int defaultSecs)
{
    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(rawValue) && int.TryParse(rawValue, out var secs) && secs > 0)
        return TimeSpan.FromSeconds(secs);
    return TimeSpan.FromSeconds(defaultSecs);
}
```

### CommandRouter.cs:21-23 — usage line without serial hint
```csharp
public static string UsageLine =>
    "usage: ./visual-relay [launch|build|test|format|screenshot|run-task|init|" +
    "install-hooks|bump-version|check|inspect|guards|audit|gen-backend-config|provision-mxc]";
```

### xunit.runner.json — the parallelism config serial mode must override
```json
{
  "parallelizeTestCollections": true,
  "maxParallelThreads": "2.0x",
  "parallelAlgorithm": "aggressive"
}
```

---

## Repro

1. **Confirm the baseline**: `NO_BUILD=1 ./visual-relay test CliSerialTestModeTests` — this fails because the test class doesn't exist yet (red-first).
2. **Confirm the extraction point**: inspect `TestRunner.cs:26-47` — all argument construction is inline.
3. **Confirm the watchdog gap**: `WatchdogTimeouts.ForTest()` always returns 60s default; a serial full suite would trip it.
4. **Confirm the UsageLine gap**: `grep 'test' tools/VisualRelay.Cli/CommandRouter.cs` shows no serial mention.
5. **Confirm the TROUBLESHOOTING gap**: `grep -i serial TROUBLESHOOTING.md` returns nothing.

---

## Needed changes (prose summary)

### TestRunner.cs

1. Extract a `public static List<string> BuildTestArgs(string testsProject, string logDir, string stem, bool noBuild, IReadOnlyList<string> cliArgs, out bool isSerial)` method from lines 26–47. The method builds the same `List<string>` that `RunAsync` currently builds inline. `isSerial` is set true when the first token ordinals-equals `"serial"` and that token is consumed.

2. Inside `BuildTestArgs`: after the optional `"serial"` consumption, apply the existing filter logic to the *remaining* tokens unchanged. Then, if `isSerial`: check whether any remaining forwarded token is exactly `"--"` and throw an `ArgumentException` with a clear message if so. Otherwise append `"--"` and `"xUnit.ParallelizeTestCollections=false"` as the final two entries.

3. In `RunAsync`: call `BuildTestArgs` instead of the inline block. Call a new `WatchdogTimeouts.ForTest(serial: isSerial)` instead of `ForTest()`. When `isSerial` is true, print `"serial mode: one collection at a time; per-test timings are trustworthy"` to stderr alongside the existing log-path lines.

### WatchdogTimeouts.cs

4. Add an overload or parameterized variant: `public static TimeSpan ForTest(bool serial)` that calls `Resolve(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("VISUAL_RELAY_TEST_TIMEOUT"), serial ? 1800 : 60)`. The existing parameterless `ForTest()` can delegate to `ForTest(serial: false)` for backward compatibility (only `CheckCommand` uses `ForTest()` outside of `TestRunner`, and it wants the 60s default).

### CommandRouter.cs

5. Update `UsageLine` to append `"  test [serial] [filter] [-- dotnet-test-args]"` or similar, making the `serial` token visible.

### TROUBLESHOOTING.md

6. Add a short section (e.g. after the hang section or as a new subsection) explaining that `./visual-relay test serial` runs test collections one at a time so per-test timings are trustworthy, useful for finding slow tests.

### New test file: `tests/VisualRelay.Tests/CliSerialTestModeTests.cs`

7. Four tests following the `CliTestLogPathsTests` / `CliWatchdogTests` pattern:
   - `[Fact]` — `"serial"` leading token produces args ending with `"--"`, `"xUnit.ParallelizeTestCollections=false"` and no `FullyQualifiedName~serial` filter.
   - `[Fact]` — `"serial", "GitCommitter"` produces both the RunSettings tail and `"--filter"`, `"FullyQualifiedName~GitCommitter"`.
   - `[Fact]` — `"GitCommitter"` alone produces args identical to today's (no RunSettings tail).
   - `[Theory]` with `[InlineData]` — `WatchdogTimeouts.ForTest(serial: true)` returns 1800s when env var is absent, and honors the env var when set (exercise `Resolve` directly with canned values).

### InternalsVisibleTo (if keeping `internal`)

8. If `BuildTestArgs` is `internal static` as the task states, add `[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo("VisualRelay.Tests")]` to `VisualRelay.Cli.csproj` or to a `AssemblyInfo.cs` in the CLI project. (Making it `public static` avoids this — all other tested types are already public — but the task says `internal`.)
